ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and legal representatives against: (i) TRACFIN PEP database (domestic politically exposed persons); (ii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (Regulation 269/2014 and successor acts); (iii) UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (iv) OFAC SDN and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications List; (v) French Ministry of Economy Asset Freeze Register (Registre national des gels); (vi) EU PEP database cross-referenced against FATF high-risk third-country list (EU Delegated Regulation 2016/1675 as amended). Enhanced due diligence (EDD) applies automatically for: PEPs, persons from FATF grey/black list jurisdictions, complex ownership structures, and any UBO with public procurement exposure. EDD includes: written source-of-funds declaration, independent verification of wealth origin, senior management approval, and annual re-screening. Screening must be documented with date, methodology, and results, retained 5 years post-relationship end (Article L.561-12 CMF).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.aml_penalties_criminal: Article 324-1 of the French Criminal Code: money laundering punishable by 5 years imprisonment and €375,000 fine (doubled for organized crime); Article L.561-49 CMF: administrative fines up to €10M or 10% of annual turnover for serious AML breaches
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ongoing_aml_reporting_obligation: Declaration of suspicion (déclaration de soupçon) to TRACFIN within 48 hours of detection; threshold-free for suspicious transactions; systematic declaration for cash transactions exceeding €10,000

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique électronique des formalités d'entreprises (INPI) – https://www.guichet-unique.inpi.fr (portal migration from Infogreffe/RNCS effective 1 January 2023, operated by INPI under Article 1 of Law 2021-1309 and Decree 2021-1506)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Article L.210-2 of the French Commercial Code mandates that corporate names and all statutory documents be drafted in French. Non-French characters (including Chinese, Arabic, Cyrillic) must be transliterated into Latin characters according to the French national transliteration standard (ISO 9 for Cyrillic, ISO 233 for Arabic, Pinyin romanization for Chinese without tone marks). The name must be distinct, non-misleading, and must not contravene public order or good morals (Article L.210-2 al.3). SAS names may include the acronym 'SAS' or 'Société par Actions Simplifiée' but the latter may be abbreviated. The name must not infringe prior trademarks (INPI trademark search mandatory under Article L.711-1 CPI).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Foundation / Fondation (requires specific decree or ministerial approval under Article L.140 of Law of 1901 or Article L.213-1 Commercial Code for endowment funds)
National / Nationale / République / France (without ministerial authorization per Article R.123-6 Commercial Code)
Charitable / Caritatif / Bienfaisance / Utilité Publique (requires ministerial recognition or RUP status)
Scientific Research / Recherche Scientifique (may require Ministry of Research approval for certain activities)
Security / Sécurité / Défense (requires Ministry of Interior/Armed Forces authorization)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of name by INPI Guichet Unique, the applicant receives a formal Notice of Rejection (notification de rejet) via the portal within 5 business days. Administrative appeal options: (1) Request for reconsideration (recours gracieux) to the INPI Director General within 2 months of notification, citing the legal basis for contestation (Article R.123-4 Commercial Code); (2) If rejected, file appeal before the competent Administrative Court (Tribunal administratif de Paris for INPI decisions) within 2 months of final rejection (Article R.421-1 Code de justice administrative); (3) Alternatively, submit a new name proposal via Guichet Unique with modified name. Name reservation (certificat de disponibilité) is valid 30 days and can be renewed once (additional 30 days) upon written request with justification. No formal extension beyond 60 days total is permitted. Upon final approval, the name is reserved for 6 months for the purpose of completing incorporation formalities.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office (domiciliation commerciale) is legally permissible for SAS under Article L.123-11-1 of the French Commercial Code, provided: (i) the domiciliation company is registered with the prefecture (Article L.123-11-2); (ii) the SAS has a genuine link to the domiciliation address (effective management, not mere mail forwarding); (iii) the lease agreement or domiciliation contract is filed with the RCS and RBE; (iv) the address is not a purely postal box (boîte postale) — operating a real office presence is required for substance. For ISIC 6430 (Endowment Management for Philanthropic and Scientific Grants), banking AML/CFT risk tier is Low_Risk_Standard, but significant charitable fund flows attract enhanced scrutiny. The ACPR and TRACFIN expect physical operational capacity for fund management, grant oversight, and governance meetings. Virtual office alone is insufficient to satisfy substance requirements for charitable endowment entities receiving public donations or tax-exempt advantages under Article 200 and 238 bis CGI (tax regime for associations/foundations of public utility).
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-High (60-75%) — SAS entities with charitable endowment activities are subject to unannounced inspections by: (i) DGFiP (tax authority) for verification of tax-exempt status and use of funds; (ii) Cour des comptes or regional audit chambers (Chambres régionales des comptes) if receiving public subsidies; (iii) TRACFIN AML inspectors upon suspicion; (iv) INPI/INSEE for periodic compliance verification of RCS data accuracy. Post-incorporation within first 18 months, a physical inspection probability of 60-75% applies for charitable/endowment SAS due to heightened AML/CFT and tax-exemption scrutiny.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), acting through the competent Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE). The principal digital portal is impots.gouv.fr. Company formation and statutory business registration are filed through the Guichet unique operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI); INSEE allocates the SIREN identifier. The French VAT identification number is issued by the DGFiP and generally has the format FR followed by a two-digit control key and the nine-digit SIREN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS must be formed and registered through the Guichet unique. The registration process transmits corporate data to the competent registries, INSEE and the tax administration. The resulting SIREN identifies the legal entity and the SIRET identifies each establishment. The company must provide its articles of association, registered-office evidence, identity and authority documents for representatives, beneficial-owner information, business activity description, bank and accounting information where requested, and the intended tax and VAT treatment. The company must submit the appropriate tax registration information to its SIE, including the commencement date, expected taxable activities, accounting period, VAT regime and intra-Community transaction status. The SIE issues or confirms the French VAT number where the entity conducts taxable transactions or elects a VAT regime. A foreign entity without a French establishment generally applies for a French VAT number through the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères or the competent DGFiP service. An entity established in another EU Member State generally does not require a French fiscal representative solely for French VAT registration; a non-EU entity normally requires an accredited French fiscal representative unless an applicable mutual-assistance arrangement removes that requirement. EU-established taxable persons may also use the applicable French OSS regime for qualifying cross-border B2C transactions, but OSS does not replace a French VAT registration when domestic registration is otherwise required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A French SAS is ordinarily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) on its taxable profits. The legal form does not create charitable or foundation tax exemption. A charitable or grant-making purpose may support specific non-profit or public-interest exemptions only where the entity satisfies the applicable statutory conditions, including non-lucrative management, absence of private profit distribution and qualifying activities. Grants and donations may be outside the scope of VAT or exempt depending on their legal and economic character, but investment management, commercial services and other taxable activities remain subject to the applicable tax rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An SAS may elect temporarily for partnership-style income taxation under the French corporate tax rules if it satisfies the statutory conditions, including qualifying ownership and management requirements, a qualifying commercial, industrial, craft or professional activity, and the applicable age and size limitations. The election is generally limited to five fiscal years and must be made within the prescribed period to the tax administration; it is not a general permanent pass-through election and may be unsuitable or unavailable for a charitable endowment model. There is no United States-style check-the-box election. French anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implement the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive framework and may deny deductions, impose inclusion or restrict relief for hybrid arrangements; they are statutory anti-avoidance rules rather than elective entity-classification mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT), administered under the French Code général des impôts and applicable European Union VAT rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: France has no single general VAT registration threshold for all taxable persons. A taxable business carrying out transactions subject to French VAT may be required to register from the first taxable transaction, particularly where it is established outside France or does not qualify for the domestic small-business exemption. The franchise en base de TVA may apply to eligible French-established businesses below the applicable annual turnover thresholds. The principal current thresholds are generally EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and certain accommodation or food activities and EUR 37,500 for services and professional activities, with tolerance thresholds generally of EUR 93,500 and EUR 41,250 respectively. Thresholds and sector-specific rules must be verified for the relevant tax year. Intra-Community acquisitions, imports, exports, reverse-charge transactions and transactions subject to special regimes can create registration or reporting obligations independently of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory domestic B2B electronic invoicing and transaction-data reporting in phases. All French VAT-taxable businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026. Mandatory issuance is scheduled from 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and certain larger groups and from 1 September 2027 for small and medium-sized enterprises and micro-enterprises, subject to statutory transitional rules. Invoices must generally be transmitted through an approved private electronic invoicing platform or the public platform designated by the French system, using structured or hybrid formats and required data fields. E-reporting applies to specified B2C and cross-border transactions. France does not generally operate a universal real-time invoice-clearance or pre-issuance digital-stamping system for ordinary commercial invoices. Public-sector invoices are submitted through Chorus Pro. Records, invoice authenticity, integrity and readability must be maintained for the statutory retention period, generally ten years for invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods shipped from France to a destination outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT under Article 262 of the French Code général des impôts, provided the exporter or an authorized intermediary can demonstrate that the goods physically left the European Union and that the transaction, exporter status and customs formalities are properly documented. The customs export declaration, MRN and electronic confirmation of exit are the principal evidence. Intra-Community supplies of goods to a VAT-identified customer in another EU Member State may qualify for the separate intra-Community supply exemption if transport, customer VAT identification, recapitulative reporting and documentary conditions are satisfied. Services are not generally described as zero-rated exports. B2B services supplied to a business established outside France are normally located outside France under the place-of-supply rules, while qualifying services supplied to EU business customers are generally subject to customer-state reverse charge. Special rules apply to immovable-property services, passenger transport, admission, events, telecommunications, electronically supplied services, financial services and other categories. A charitable or grant-making purpose does not itself establish export VAT exemption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration submitted through the applicable French or EU electronic customs system
Electronic confirmation of exit or equivalent customs exit result
Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, customer, goods, value, delivery terms and destination
Packing list and transport documentation, including bill of lading, airway bill, CMR or equivalent
Evidence linking the goods, invoice and customs declaration, including purchase orders and logistics records
Proof of payment or contractual consideration where relevant to substantiate the transaction
VAT records and export reporting records supporting the exemption
For intra-Community supplies, the customer VAT identification number, transport evidence and required recapitulative statement

Inward remittance certificate only where required by a bank, grant condition, financing arrangement or another jurisdiction; France does not generally require an inward remittance certificate as a statutory condition for export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation requirement for export VAT relief. French VAT exemption depends principally on the legal conditions and documentary proof of export or the applicable place-of-supply rule. If the tax administration rejects the exemption, it may assess the VAT that should have been charged, applicable late-payment interest, and penalties. Deliberate or materially negligent misstatements may attract tax penalties, including a 40% surcharge for deliberate failure and an 80% surcharge for fraudulent manoeuvres or abusive conduct, subject to the applicable statutory facts and procedural safeguards. Late-payment interest is generally calculated at the statutory monthly rate applicable to the assessment period. False customs declarations may trigger customs reassessment, customs penalties, loss of preferential treatment and, in serious cases, criminal liability under French and Union customs law. Fraudulent VAT claims, fabricated export evidence or unjustified input-VAT refunds may result in repayment of the refund, denial of input-tax deduction, tax penalties, recovery proceedings and criminal prosecution. Documentary records should be retained for the applicable accounting and tax limitation periods, commonly ten years for invoices and supporting commercial records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) is the central bank and the designated balance-of-payments statistics authority for France. Foreign-exchange and capital-movement policy is implemented by the Banque de France in coordination with the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance, while the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) is the consolidated banking supervisor.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France, as a Eurosystem member, operates a fully convertible currency regime; the euro is freely transferable and there are no exchange controls on current-account or capital-account transactions for EEA/OECD counterparties. Capital movements are liberalised pursuant to Article 63 TFEU and Articles L151-1 to L153-1 of the French Monetary and Financial Code. No prior approval is required for routine capital injections, grant disbursements, or profit remittances; residual restrictions apply only to inward direct investments from non-EEA investors in regulated or strategic sectors and to exceptional safeguard measures. Profit remittances by a French SAS are lawful once tax compliance is satisfied; dividends paid to non-resident shareholders may be subject to withholding tax in the range of 25%-30% unless reduced by a double-tax treaty or exempt under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive. For a private charitable foundation, the distribution of grants is not a profit remittance but a non-commercial transfer made in the public interest, and should be documented as such to avoid recharacterisation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no mandatory surrender or statutory conversion ratio on export proceeds. Export receipts may be retained freely in euros or foreign currency and may be used for offshore disbursements without Bank of France approval. However, French resident entities must report cross-border transactions to Banque de France for balance-of-payments purposes when the aggregate value of their monthly transactions with non-resident counterparties exceeds €12,500. The declaration must be filed electronically through the Banque de France BOP reporting channel within 20 business days after the end of the calendar month in which the transactions occurred. Export proceeds held on accounts with foreign correspondents must also be reflected in the resident entity's balance-of-payments position reporting.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Medium for auxiliary settlement flows; Low for core endowment custody and capital escrow. French or EEA-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) authorised by ACPR under PSD2 may provide euro IBANs, SEPA payment accounts, multi-currency wallets, and cross-border collections. Their principal legal constraint is that they cannot grant credit, are not deposit-taking credit institutions, and cannot offer the same statutory protection as a bank operating escrow account. EMIs such as Qonto, Wise Business, Airwallex, and Currencycloud may be used as pre-funded operating sub-accounts for grant disbursements, provided that the main treasury account is held with a Tier-1 credit institution. UK-licensed EMIs no longer benefit from EU passporting after Brexit and require either a French/EEA licence or an ACPR branch authorisation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no universal statutory requirement that a director must appear physically in France; French AML law permits remote identity verification through accredited video-KYC when supported by qualified eIDAS-signature evidence. Nevertheless, Tier-1 French banks commonly require at least one signatory director or an appointed legal representative with a power of attorney to attend a physical onboarding interview in France, particularly when non-resident shareholders or foreign UBOs are present. Where physical attendance is impracticable, banks may accept a notarised power of attorney issued by a French notary or consulate, combined with a videoconference interview and complete documentary evidence, provided that all UBOs are assessed as low-risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Company form (SAS) does not match the claimed 'private charitable foundation' status; the bank requires proof of the endowment/public-interest legal framework.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised by-laws (statuts constitutifs), a less-than-three-months K-bis extract, SIREN/SIRET registration, endowment deed or constitution act, declaration to the Préfecture or recognition decree from the Conseil d'État where the entity is 'reconnue d'utilité publique', board resolutions approving the banking relationship, and confirmation that the entity has no commercial purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large cross-border capital injection or donation from a foreign donor within the first 12 months of account opening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds package: notarised gift deed or donation agreement, donor bank reference and account history, origin of wealth (inheritance, sale, liquidation, or income), donor identity documents and corporate registry extract, tax residence certificate, board resolution accepting the endowment, and a forward grant programme budget consistent with the declared philanthropic purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or indirect UBOs detected through a multi-layer corporate chain, creating opacity risks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO declaration from the French Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs, verified identity and address of each natural-person beneficial owner, full corporate structure chart, registry extracts for every intermediate entity, CRS/FATCA tax self-certification, and a written confirmation that no bearer shares, nominee arrangements, or shell structures exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regular grant disbursements to beneficiaries in high-risk jurisdictions or to natural persons, which could trigger misuse-of-banking-products or money-laundering red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written grant policy, call-for-proposals documentation, grant agreements, KYC/AML due diligence on each final beneficiary, project progress reports, expense receipts, negative UN/EU sanctions screening results, and a signed 'no-redistribution / own-use' declaration. A complete grant disbursement register must be maintained and made available to the bank's AML and compliance units upon request.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound endowment contributions should be effected by SWIFT MT103 from the donor's bank to the French Tier-1 bank using the receiving entity's BIC/IBAN. For euro payments within SEPA, a SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) may be used and must include the ordering customer's name and address, the foundation's full legal name, and a purpose reference identifying the transaction as a charitable endowment contribution. Where a payment category is required, the ISO 20022 Category Purpose Code 'CHAR' is appropriate, supplemented by a free-text reference such as 'gift/endowment contribution'. Because France does not require exchange-control approval, the principal compliance requirement is Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting: all inbound capital flows must be aggregated when the monthly cross-border total exceeds €12,500 and declared through the electronic BOP channel. The receiving bank will also perform sanctions screening and source-of-funds verification prior to crediting the escrow account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border grant disbursements and trade settlements should be cleared through SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers with full beneficiary name, IBAN/account number, BIC, address, and purpose code. Euro payments within the SEPA zone are cleared as SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT) without FX conversion; large or non-EEA payments require correspondent banking or TARGET2 settlement where the beneficiary bank is directly TARGET2-connected. For commercial letters of credit, the French issuing bank operates through SWIFT MT700; amendments are transmitted by MT707, confirmations by MT710, and documentary collections by MT400/MT910 with MT202 cover when required. The foundation may use the same SWIFT rails to make grant payments directly to foreign beneficiaries; no FX surrender or conversion applies because the underlying activity is non-exporting and all disbursements are charitably motivated.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards with an authorised credit institution, limited to known grant or endowment currency exposures and documented under an ISDA 1998 FX or 2002 Master Agreement.
FX swaps (swap de change) used to convert and re-convert liquidity between the euro functional currency and grant payout currencies.
Cross-currency swaps referencing EUR and USD, CHF, or GBP for long-term endowment liabilities or multi-year grant commitments.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies when the primary currency is not deliverable onshore; permitted only for hedging identifiable exposures and never for speculative positions.

Plain vanilla FX options (European-style calls or puts) purchased with a one-off non-leveraged premium, provided the bank's suitability assessment confirms the foundation has adequate derivative knowledge or the services of a dedicated investment adviser.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts by shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the Société par Actions Simplifiée
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each financial year, unless extended by court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure may result in a court injunction, daily coercive penalty, and liability of the legal representative; no automatic statutory strike-off deadline applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts and management report, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registry of the Commercial Court through the Guichet Unique managed by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of the accounts, or within two months where filed electronically; exemptions and confidentiality options may apply to qualifying small or micro companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a court injunction and coercive penalties; the legal representative may incur a civil fine of up to EUR 1,500, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance. Persistent non-compliance may support administrative or judicial removal procedures, but no automatic strike-off timetable applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return No. 2065 and financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by the second business day after 1 May for a 31 December year-end; generally within three months after the financial year-end for other year-ends, subject to the applicable electronic-filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may generate a 10% surcharge, late-payment interest, tax audit exposure, and additional penalties for inaccurate or incomplete declarations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and update of registered beneficial-owner information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registry of the competent Commercial Court through the Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: France does not generally require a separate annual no-change confirmation; changes must be reported promptly and generally within 30 days after the relevant change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintain accurate beneficial-owner information may result in formal notice, court-ordered compliance, criminal penalties for responsible persons, and restrictions or consequences affecting the company's registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Update of corporate registers following share transfers, director changes, or governance resolutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records; relevant changes requiring publicity are filed through the Guichet Unique and published in the applicable legal-announcement channel
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Immediately after the relevant corporate event; public-registration changes are generally filed within one month unless a specific rule provides otherwise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unrecorded or unfiled changes may be unenforceable against third parties, create director liability, and trigger registry correction orders or monetary penalties. Share transfers must also comply with the SAS articles and applicable transfer formalities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual auditor report and statutory audit, where mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and, where required, the Registry of the Commercial Court with the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit procedures must be completed before shareholder approval of the annual accounts; the auditor's report is presented with the accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint a required commissaire aux comptes may result in judicial appointment, criminal sanctions, invalidity or challenge of regulated corporate actions, and director liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual social and payroll reporting compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French social-security authorities through the Déclaration Sociale Nominative system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Primarily monthly rather than annual; year-end payroll, tax, and social reconciliations must be completed within the applicable reporting timetable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or inaccurate reporting may generate social-security reassessments, late-payment charges, penalties, and payroll tax audit exposure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SAS generally must appoint a commissaire aux comptes when it exceeds at least two of three thresholds at the financial year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet assets, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Appointment may also be required for certain groups, control relationships, regulated activities, or specific statutory circumstances. A charitable purpose or grant-making activity does not by itself eliminate the audit rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French generally accepted accounting principles under the Autorité des Normes Comptables framework apply to statutory accounts. IFRS may apply to consolidated accounts where legally permitted or required. An SAS does not automatically constitute a French foundation or endowment fund; any separate foundation or regulated philanthropic status requires independent legal qualification and authorization.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no general annual UBO confirmation filing in France. The company must maintain accurate beneficial-owner information and file an amendment generally within 30 days after any change in ownership, voting rights, control, or beneficial-owner particulars. Share transfers must be recorded in the SAS share-transfer and shareholder records, with corresponding UBO and public-registration updates where control changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members or shareholder account records and share-transfer records
Register of Directors and corporate officers
Minute book or authenticated record of shareholder and collective decisions
Register of beneficial owners or accessible beneficial-owner filing records
Annual accounts, management reports, auditor reports, and supporting corporate approvals

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 3,000-10,000 for a small SAS subject to statutory audit; complex, regulated, or group entities may incur materially higher fees

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) on net taxable profits; 15% reduced rate applies to the first EUR 42,500 of annual taxable profit for qualifying small companies (turnover ceiling EUR 10 million, 75% individual ownership, fully paid-up capital).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Research tax credit (CIR) at 30% on eligible R&D expenses up to EUR 100 million; Innovation tax credit (CII) at 20% capped at EUR 400,000; patronage (mécénat) deduction of 60% of qualifying charitable gifts up to 0.5% of turnover; a genuinely recognised fondation d'entreprise or fonds de dotation holding the endowment may benefit from the non-commercial exemption under Articles 206-1-b and 207 CGI, subject to prior recognition by the Conseil d'État or prefectoral approval; tax losses are carried forward indefinitely with an annual absorption cap of EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1,000,000, and a one-year carry-back credit capped at EUR 1,000,000 (numeric field 0 encodes the absence of a statutory time limit).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire No. 2065 (Cerfa No. 15950) ‘Déclaration de résultats’ together with the liasse fiscale (schedules 2052–2059 and 2061), filed exclusively by electronic transmission (EDI/EFI) through the impots.gouv.fr professional portal; entities benefiting from the charitable non-commercial regime alternatively file Form 2070 series.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; once per fiscal year, irrespective of quarterly instalment payments of corporate income tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return due within 3 months of the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year fiscal year ending 31 December, the electronic filing deadline is 3 May of the following year (extended to the next business day where the 3rd falls on a non-working day); non-calendar fiscal years are due three months after the closing date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIREN, SIRET, APE/NAF code, legal form, corporate capital, registered office, and beneficial-owner declaration reference (Article 1649 AC CGI).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the SIRET of the French permanent establishment as the place of taxation; do not file in France in the absence of a PE; non-resident beneficial owners must be disclosed separately in the beneficial-ownership register.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065, Block B (Résultat) – Line GA / Line GB
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (GA) or net deficit (GB) of the fiscal year after application of carried-forward losses, charitable endowment deductions, and CIR/CII credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident SAS reports only French-source profits attributable to its French PE; foreign tableau income from the endowment portfolio is excluded unless booked through the PE; foreign tax credits are claimed in Schedule 2065-SD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 2058-A – Lines WE (taux réduit) / WH (taux normal)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apportionment of taxable profit: first EUR 42,500 of profit taxed at 15% (WE) and the remainder at 25% (WH); CIR and CII credits are then offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 15% reduced rate is available only for profits of a French PE of a small-enterprise whose worldwide turnover does not exceed EUR 10 million; the PE manager must certify compliance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet and income statement: endowment portfolio securities, receivables, grant commitments, capital funds, and financial income from management of philanthropic assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose only assets and flows of the French PE; intercompany receivables with foreign grantors or investment managers must be supported by written contractual documentation to avoid recharacterisation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Return used where the entity or its separately recognised foundation arm claims exemption for non-commercial philanthropic activities; reports incoming gifts, grant distributions, and administrative expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident trustees or foreign grantors must attach evidence of treaty residence and source; exempt activity must never generate commercial profit distributions to founders.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge of 10% of the tax due, increased to 40% if the return is not filed within 30 days of a formal demand and to 80% in cases of fraudulent conduct; monthly late-payment interest of 0.20% accrues from the statutory deadline; fixed fines of EUR 150 to EUR 750 apply to missing schedules or annexes; criminal prosecution under Article 1741 CGI is possible for deliberate omission.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident beneficial owners (Article 119 bis 2 CGI); dividends qualifying under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and Article 145 CGI (minimum 10% shareholding held for at least 2 years) are exempt at source (0%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a treaty-reduced rate at source, the non-resident beneficial owner must lodge Form 5000/5001/5002/5003, a certificate of tax residence (TRC), and a beneficial-ownership declaration with the French paying agent before distribution; if tax is withheld in excess, a refund claim must be filed within 2 years of the date of the levy (Article R.196-1 LPF) with supporting TRC and certification; EU resident companies may substitute the simplified EU attestation procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest on arm's-length loans to non-residents is not subject to French withholding tax (0% domestic rate; 0% under most treaties; a 75% withholding applies to payments routed to non-cooperative jurisdictions under Articles 238 A and 119 bis CGI); royalty payments for patents and assimilated IP rights are subject to the statutory 33.33% withholding under Article 1678 bis CGI, reduced to 0% between associated EU companies under the Interest and Royalties Directive (25% shareholding) and to 5% between France and the United States on patent and trademark royalties; copyright and software royalties are generally exempt from French withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Master File and French Local File (Article L.13 AA Code des procédures fiscales) are mandatory when the French entity's annual turnover or gross assets exceed EUR 400,000,000, or when the entity is controlled by, or controls, a group exceeding that threshold; country-by-country reporting applies to consolidated groups with EUR 750,000,000 or more of annual revenue; simplified documentation applies to medium-sized groups.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines hierarchy with most-appropriate-method analysis
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no standalone Economic Substance Regulation regime comparable to ESR jurisdictions; substance is enforced through the general anti-abuse rule (abus de droit, Article L.64 LPF), the ATAD GAAR (Article 205 A CGI), CFC provisions (Article 209 B CGI), treaty anti-abuse clauses, and the requirement of a genuine economic purpose. A private charitable endowment managed by an SAS must maintain a French governing board, local investment and grant-approval processes, minutes, and complete records at its registered office; otherwise the tax administration may disregard the entity, reclassify the endowment's investment income as commercial profit, and apply the 80% abuse penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully failing to file Form 2065, hiding endowment investment income, or presenting materially false financial statements to the tax authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years under Article 1741 CGI, increased to EUR 2,000,000 and 7 years when committed in an organised group or through offshore concealment; civil tax penalties of 40% (bad faith) or 80% (fraudulent manoeuvres) plus 0.20% monthly late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president and directors face criminal liability for fraud; the tax authorities may impose joint personal liability under Article L.267 LPF for taxes arising from fraudulent conduct, order freezing of personal assets, prohibitions on managing commercial entities, travel bans, and imprisonment upon conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing endowment income or corpus to founders, directors, or related persons; conducting profit-seeking commercial activity under the philanthropic veil; failure to disburse mandatory grants; operating as a cash-box without genuine grant-making functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withdrawal of the charitable exemption with retroactive effect, reclassification of all accumulated income as commercial profit taxable at 25% or 15%, application of the 80% bad-faith penalty under Article 1729 b CGI, restitution of tax credits, and dissolution proceedings by the competent prefecture or public prosecutor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil liability for restitution of misappropriated assets, disqualification from managing any foundation or company, personal risk of the action en comblement du passif under Article L.651-2 Code de commerce if mismanagement caused the entity's insolvency, and criminal conviction for abus de confiance (up to 5 years imprisonment and EUR 375,000 fine).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the mandatory declaration of beneficial owners under Article 1649 AC CGI; failure to report suspicious transactions or unusual grant flows to TRACFIN; omissions in the AML risk assessment of donors and grant recipients.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fixed administrative fines up to EUR 20,000 per missing beneficial-ownership filing; AML penalties for legal entities up to EUR 375,000 per violation (up to EUR 5,000,000 for aggravated money laundering); prohibition of banking payment rails (Bank Wire, Grant Distribution) and loss of the required statutory licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally exposed to criminal prosecution for money laundering (up to 5 years imprisonment and EUR 375,000 fine), travel bans, asset freezes, and forfeiture of personal property; repeated AML breaches trigger automatic disqualification from corporate office.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Abuse and Artificial Offshore Structures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging or paying non-arm's-length fees to foreign related entities, booking endowment fees to shell companies in zero-tax jurisdictions, undocumentated intercompany loans, or artificially shifting French investment income to treaty-haven entities without genuine substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of profits under French arm's-length rules with 40% bad-faith penalty, 80% abuse-of-law penalty where the arrangement lacks genuine commercial purpose, 0.20% monthly late-payment interest, fines of EUR 15,000 per missing transfer-pricing document, and denial of treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorised or benefited from the abusive scheme may be joined to the tax debt under Article L.267 LPF, ordered to replenish corporate assets personally, subjected to international travel bans, and imprisoned upon criminal conviction for tax fraud; extradition risk applies where the arrangement involves non-cooperative jurisdictions.
